text:
Alex: Noticed a new perf hotspot on canary this morning. Mixed batches with a small long tail (~5-12% >1k) cause router to choose long-path kernels and short requests get slammed by KV growth/evictions. Seen during a 02:40 deploy window. :warning:

Mei: Can you paste the kernel selection trace + a very small profiler snippet? Need to confirm whether it's a router heuristic or runtime fallback churn.

Alex: Trimmed trace and profiler extract below:
```
[batch] id=0xca11
composition: short=72%, mid=20%, long=8%
router_choice: unified_kernel=fused_attn_long_opt
observed: short_token_exec ~120ms (baseline ~30ms)
kv_evictions: batch=21 (burst at prefill->decode handoff)
cuda: smem_bw_throttle ~16% during handoff
callstack: routing/selector.cc:line 178 -> prefill/kv_slab.cc:evict_range -> kernels/fused_attn_long_opt.cu
```
Router bias toward long path because of long tail. That expands prefill KV allocations and thrashes small entries.

Lucas: This pattern is distinct from previous regressions: eviction count much higher. We only log mean seqlen today which hides the multimodal mix.

Sam: Short-term mitigation ideas:
- Add a "short-priority" soft rule: if short_frac >= 0.70 prefer short kernel. Allow per-request fallback for long requests that need long ops.
- Add metric batch_slen_histogram and kernel_choice_by_batch to measure.

Anya: Medium term: change allocator to support per-request KV reservation for tiny prefills (seqlen <=64). That prevents large-prefill eviction but requires slab tuning + GC semantics.

Mei: We should also try a utility-based kernel pick: score kernels by expected p95 impact across requests in the batch (not just throughput). That would be a change to the autotuner scoring function.

Alex: For immediate response I'm planning a canary rule. Config diff:
```
router.rules:
  - id: slen_short_bias_v1
    condition: batch.short_frac >= 0.70
    action:
      prefer_kernel: short_fast_v4
      allow_per_request_fallback: true
      sample_traces_on_mismatch: 1/100
      hysteresis_ms: 200
```
This biases toward short kernel while allowing longs to requeue on a compatible path. Hysteresis avoids flapping.

infra-bot: deploy-canary started: pool canary-west update at 2291110120 by ops-ci

Sam: Test matrix for canary run:
- Synthetic 45m workload 70/30 short/long mix, control vs candidate
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 short, p50/p95/p99 long, kv_evictions_per_batch, kernel_mismatch_rate, gpu_mem_pressure, OOM_count
- Accept if short p95 drops >=40% and long p99 increases <=15% and no new OOMs.

Alex: Running synthetic now. Will stream results. Also added a tiny nvprof sampling for batches with mismatch.

(10m later)
Alex: Early canary results:
- short p95: control=138ms -> candidate=38ms
- short p99: control=412ms -> candidate=104ms
- kv_evictions_per_batch: control=2.6 -> candidate=0.7 (~73% drop)
- long p95: control=1.22s -> candidate=1.33s (+9%)
- kernel_mismatch_rate increased ~5% but fallbacks handled requests.

Mei: Good initial signal. Upload profiler tar and nvprof snippets to perf bucket and add links on the new dashboard.

Alex: Uploaded artifacts: https://s3.redwood/perf/2291110200/slen_shortbias_canary_v1.tar.gz

Anya: I'll write the RFC for per-request KV reservation as a medium-term fix (allocator changes + perf model). Include expected memory overhead and eviction simulation.

Lucas: Rollout plan: A/B 12% for 4h -> 50% for 2h -> ramp to full if no regressions. Add auto-rollback if kv_evictions_per_batch > baseline * 1.5 or OOM_count > 0.

Sam: Also add a sampled "kernel_decision_debug" trace for batches where router picks a kernel that the profiler later marks suboptimal so we can improve the autotune scoring.

Alex: Action items:
- Alex: promote A/B 12% and run overnight extended synthetic tests
- Mei: add dashboards (batch_slen_histogram, kv_evictions_by_bucket, kernel_choice_count, kernel_mismatch_samples)
- Lucas: prepare rollback runbook and automated alert thresholds
- Anya: start RFC for KV reservation + allocator changes
- Sam: validate trace sampling quotas and retention

infra-bot: A/B rollout scheduled at 2291110300

Alex: Thanks y'all. Reopen thread if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
